'''Kostiantyn Merkuriyovych Sytnyk''' ({{langx|uk|Костянтин Меркурійович Ситник}}; 3 June 1926 – 22 July 2017) was a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] and [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] scientist and academician, a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] who in 1970-2003 was director of the Botanic Institute of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine. Sytnyk also worked as a politician, and served as the [[Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada]] of the [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic]] from 1980 to 1985.

== Early life and scientific career ==
Sytnyk was born on 3 June 1926 in the city of [[Luhansk]], which was then part of the [[Ukrainian SSR]] in the [[Soviet Union]].<ref name="kyiv">{{cite web |title=80-річчя академіка НАН України К.М. Ситника |url=https://www.botany.kiev.ua/ksytnik.htm |website=www.botany.kiev.ua |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sytnyk Konstantyn M. |url=https://www.old.nas.gov.ua/EN/PersonalSite/Pages/Biography.aspx?PersonID=0000012280 |website=old.nas.gov.ua |access-date=16 February 2026 |language=uk-UA}}</ref> In 1949, he graduated from the Luhansk Pedagogigcal Institute, and afterwords he began working as an assistant at the institute before in 1950 beginning to work at the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].<ref name="kyiv" /> In 1962, he was promoted to Head of the Scientific-Organizational Department and in 1966 to Chief Scientific Secretary, before in 1970 being appointed Director of the Botanic Institute.<ref name="kyiv" /> Simultaneously, he was an Academician-Secretary of General Biology from 1972 to 1984 and Vice-President and later First Vice-President of NASU from 1974 to 1988.<ref name="kyiv" />

During his time at the institute, he primarily worrked on genetic and cellular engineering of plants in Ukraine, phythormonal regulations, and he co-discovered the biparental inheritance of plasmogens.<ref name="kyiv" /> He also helped author the experiment that sent [[Leonid Kadenyuk]] to space, and studied the genus [[Achillea]].<ref name="kyiv" /> For these activities, he was awarded the [[USSR State Prize]] and the Ukrainian SSR State Prize.<ref name="kyiv" />
